title: Exact deletion interlacing for Fisk's Toeplitz-minor transform through five variables
oneLine: Exact positive-coefficient Bezout certificates prove real negative roots and strict arbitrary-deletion interlacing for Fisk's 3x3 Toeplitz-minor transform through five positive alphabet entries; the all-degree and zero-boundary problems remain open.
abstract: This anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed computer-assisted finite theorem candidate addresses AIM-ANALYSIS-0142. For a positive alphabet rho of size n, let F_rho(t) be the sum of the rectangular Schur polynomials s_(3^k)(rho) times t^k. The candidate proves that F_rho has n simple negative roots for 0 <= n <= 5 and that, for 2 <= n <= 5, deleting any chosen alphabet entry gives strict interlacing, with the larger polynomial supplying the two outer roots. The proof reduces arbitrary deletion by symmetry, constructs a signed Bezout matrix, and proves all leading principal minors positive by exact positive monomial expansions. The degree-five certificate contains 61,192 terms across five minors and is regenerated byte-for-byte by public CI. The package also preserves failed structural routes, corrected exact searches, hostile certificate mutations, a supplied Major Revision review, a producer-coordinated five-role review and one bounded exact-byte confirmation. Fisk's all-degree conjecture, zero-boundary cases, degree six beyond the first three minors, independent reconstruction, formal verification, external specialist review, novelty and priority remain open or unassessed.
narration: Steve Fisk asked whether a transformation built from three by three Toeplitz minors always preserves real negative roots. This anonymous, unrefereed candidate proves a finite part of that problem. Start with at most five positive numbers and form a polynomial whose coefficients are rectangular Schur polynomials. The resulting polynomial has only simple negative roots. If any one input number is deleted, the smaller polynomial's roots sit strictly between those of the larger polynomial. The proof uses a Bezout matrix, a classical device that turns interlacing into positivity of matrix minors. For five inputs, the five required minors expand into sixty-one thousand one hundred and ninety-two exact positive terms. The public replay regenerates those terms, compares every deterministic certificate byte, checks the sign convention, and rejects both a negative mutation and a subtler positive but incorrect mutation. This is a finite theorem candidate through five positive entries. It does not solve Fisk's all-degree conjecture, does not cover inputs on the zero boundary, and does not claim independent verification, external specialist review, peer review, novelty or priority. The synthetic voice is a communication aid, not additional mathematical evidence.

keyResults: For every positive alphabet rho of size 0 through 5, the polynomial F_rho(t) = sum s_(3^k)(rho)t^k has exactly n simple negative roots.
For every positive alphabet of size 2 through 5, deleting any chosen entry gives strict root interlacing, with the larger polynomial supplying both outer roots.
All five degree-five leading Bezout minors have positive monomial coefficients; their exact certificate streams contain 15, 771, 8,790, 29,460 and 22,156 terms.
Fresh public replay regenerates the degree-five certificates byte-for-byte and rejects both non-positive and positive-but-semantically-wrong certificate mutations.
Degree six is checked only through the first three leading minors, and Fisk's all-degree conjecture and zero-boundary cases remain open.

These establish public availability, package integrity, producer replay and the stated finite certificate—not the all-degree or zero-boundary conjecture, independent reconstruction, formal verification, external specialist review, peer review, novelty or priority.
statusDetail: Anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed computer-assisted finite theorem candidate at internal PASS_WITH_NOTES with no residual or new P0/P1 findings in the final exact-byte confirmation. The finite theorem is a written Bezout-interlacing argument supported by complete positive coefficient streams through five positive alphabet entries. Symmetry covers deletion of any chosen entry. The exhaustive small grid and seeded degree-16-through-40 search are non-load-bearing reconnaissance, not evidence for the universal claim. Degree six has only its first three leading minors certified. Inputs with a zero entry, degree drops, collision limits needed for the unrestricted parent formulation, Fisk's all-degree conjecture, independent reconstruction, proof-assistant formalization, external specialist review, journal peer review, exhaustive novelty assessment and priority adjudication remain open or unassessed.

semanticBridge.description: The package fixes the signed Bezout convention, maps F_(X,y) and F_X to a symmetric matrix, proves that positivity of all leading minors makes that matrix positive definite, and invokes the matching strict-interlacing criterion. Complete term streams bind the degree-five coefficient claim to the exact computation.
remainingRisks: The finite proof and classical interlacing bridge have not been reconstructed by an unaffiliated specialist.
Positive coefficient expansions may fail at a higher degree even if the parent conjecture remains true by another mechanism.
Strict positivity on the open orthant does not by itself settle zero entries, degree drops or multiple-root limits.
The targeted literature and GitHub search may miss differently phrased, unindexed or unpublished prior work.
